rootCauses: A whole-animal silhouette plate overlapped the radial trunk; its outline could protrude from front and top views.
A shared width formula produced blunt sections and tail bulges.
Side-projected eye and gill pixels stretched over the dorsal surface; a narrow replacement UV strip also made a visible seam during review and was replaced.
The review's generic sine-wave motion did not match the game's species-specific motion.
The game's legacy top-view repair rewrites positions and UVs, which must not be applied to the newly sculpted volume assets.

changes.wholeAnimalPlate: removed from these 153 forms; thin separate anatomical fins remain
changes.body: monotone width interpolation, smoothed cross-sections, welded crown normals, solid bills for billfish
changes.texture: continuous radial body chart plus separate fin chart in one embedded 512px base-color atlas
changes.material: nonmetal metallic-roughness PBR; authored values retained by the game for V3 assets
changes.rig: smooth spine influences and flexible paired-fin tips; morays retain the standard ten bones but have no invented paired fins
changes.runtime: new-family anguilliform, tail-dominant and fin-propelled profiles, phase-continuous clock; legacy top-view UV repair bypassed for tagged V3 GLBs
changes.review: eight camera directions plus three swim phases available per model; preview imports the game's motion source

remaining: Nine specialised forms (seahorse, skate, goosefish, each fry/juvenile/adult) retain their existing geometry and need separate sculpting review.
One side painting does not define the unseen surfaces: dorsal, ventral and opposite-side markings are reconstructed, not scanned anatomy.
Mouth cavities, opercula and fin-ray microgeometry are not fully individually sculpted; the assets are not claimed as photoreal final models.
Swimming profiles are artistic kinematic approximations, not hydrodynamic simulation; game activation remains disabled pending visual approval.
